sentences.en: I can see them being worried that if somebody goes off the cuff, they offend the queen, that

sentences.en: You know, there's lots of reasons this might have happened.

sentences.zh: 嗯，谢谢你，克里斯。

sentences.en: This is the sound of the longest escalator in the United States.
sentences.zh: 这是全美国最长的自动扶梯的声音。

sentences.en: It's at Wheaton Station, which is a stop on Washington, D.C.'s metro subway system.
sentences.zh: 它位于惠顿站，这是华盛顿特区地铁系统的一个车站。

sentences.en: The escalator is 230 feet long, and it takes about three minutes to travel from top to bottom.
sentences.zh: 这座自动扶梯长230英尺，从顶部到底部大约需要乘行三分钟。

sentences.en: 99PI's intern Olivia Green lives in D.C., and she's going to tell you about this escalator
sentences.zh: 99PI的实习生奥利维亚·格林住在华盛顿特区，她将向大家介绍这座自动扶梯

sentences.en: and some of the lore surrounding the metro station that it's a part of
sentences.zh: 以及环绕着它所在的地铁站的一些传说

sentences.en: in the length of time it takes for her to ride the escalator.
sentences.zh: 就在她乘坐扶梯的这段时间内。

sentences.en: So, here's Olivia.
sentences.zh: 那么，有请奥利维亚。

sentences.en: I'm a regular metro commuter, but standing here is always kind of an eerie experience.
sentences.zh: 我是一名经常坐地铁的通勤族，但站在这里总是有一种诡异的体验。

sentences.en: In addition to the sounds of the machines and just how deep the tunnel goes,
sentences.zh: 除了机器的轰鸣声以及隧道有多深之外，

sentences.en: if you look up, the walls are curved, gray, and stark-looking.
sentences.zh: 如果你抬头看，墙壁是呈弧形的，灰色的，看起来十分严峻。

sentences.en: Engineers chose to build this particular station so deep because the rock in this area is especially soft,
sentences.zh: 工程师们选择把这个特殊的车站建得这么深，是因为这一带的岩石特别软，

sentences.en: so they needed to dig the train tunnels and more solid rock further down.
sentences.zh: 所以他们需要把列车隧道挖到更深处那些更坚固的岩石中。

sentences.en: The tunnel's visual inspiration came from a team of architects led by a man named Harry Weiss
sentences.zh: 隧道的视觉灵感来自于一个建筑师团队，由一个名叫哈里·韦斯的人领导，

sentences.en: back in the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 那是在20世纪60年代。

sentences.en: So, prior to taking on metro, Weiss had not worked on a subway system before.
sentences.zh: 因此，在接手地铁项目之前，韦斯以前并没有参与过地铁系统的设计。

sentences.en: This is Zachary Schrag, a historian who studied the Washington metro system.
sentences.zh: 这位是扎卡里·施拉格，一位研究华盛顿地铁系统的历史学家。

sentences.en: And so, as part of this contract, he managed to get a first-class round-the-world trip,
sentences.zh: 因此，作为这份合同的一部分，他设法获得了一次一流的环球旅行，

sentences.en: spending a lot of time in Western Europe, but also in the Soviet Union, I believe in Japan,
sentences.zh: 花了很多时间在西欧，但也去了苏联，如果我没记错的话还有日本，

sentences.en: looking at subway systems and sketching them rapidly and trying to think about
sentences.zh: 去考察地铁系统并迅速勾勒草图，同时试着思考

sentences.en: what parts of them could be adapted to Washington.
sentences.zh: 它们的哪些部分可以应用到华盛顿。

sentences.en: Weiss was inspired by those train systems from around the world,
sentences.zh: 韦斯受到世界各地那些列车系统的启发，

sentences.en: and he ended up designing these vaulted underground stations with coffered ceilings
sentences.zh: 他最终设计出了这些带有密肋天花板的拱形地下车站

sentences.en: that look kind of like a waffle.
sentences.zh: 看起来有点像华夫饼。

sentences.en: The stations are lit with hidden lights that cast dramatic shadows.
sentences.zh: 车站里亮着隐藏的灯光，投射出戏剧性的阴影。

sentences.en: Harry Weiss rightly gets tremendous credit for the overall appearance of Metro.
sentences.zh: 哈里·韦斯因地铁的整体外观而获得了巨大的声誉，这是实至名归的。

sentences.en: It's unforgettable appearance, really.
sentences.zh: 那是一个令人难忘的外观，真的。

sentences.en: But it's important to understand that he was the leader of a team,
sentences.zh: 但重要的是要明白，他是团队的领导者，

sentences.en: and a very crucial member of that team was a lighting designer named William Lamb.
sentences.zh: 而该团队中非常关键的一员是一位名叫威廉·兰姆的灯光设计师。

sentences.en: Lamb was responsible for the lights that shine upwards and illuminate the vault,
sentences.zh: 兰姆负责那些向上照射并照亮拱顶的灯光，

sentences.en: turning it into a kind of underground sky.
sentences.zh: 将其变成了一种地下天空。

sentences.en: I think what Weiss was trying to do was to make the stations
sentences.zh: 我认为韦斯当时想要做的是把这些车站

sentences.en: seem like a little bit of the outdoors underground.
sentences.zh: 打造得有点像地下的户外环境。

sentences.en: So the vault is a bit like the sky,
sentences.zh: 所以拱顶有点像天空，

sentences.en: the granite edges on the platforms might resemble the curbs of a sidewalk.
sentences.zh: 站台上的花岗岩边缘可能类似于人行道的路缘。

sentences.en: But as I ride the escalator,
sentences.zh: 但当我乘坐自动扶梯时，

sentences.en: I can't help but feel like the overall effect of this design isn't always reassuring.
sentences.zh: 我总觉得这种设计的整体效果并不总是让人感到安心。

sentences.en: It's kind of spooky, and I don't think I'm the only one who feels this way.
sentences.zh: 这有点诡异，而且我觉得有这种感觉的不止我一个人。

sentences.en: In fact, the DC metro system has inspired quite a bit of extraterrestrial lore.
sentences.zh: 事实上，华盛顿特区的地铁系统引发了不少关于外星人的传说。

sentences.en: You can see hints of it in stations across the city,
sentences.zh: 你可以在全市的车站里看到一些端倪，

sentences.en: like small tags of flying saucers on the outsides of stations,
sentences.zh: 比如车站外墙上印着的小飞碟标签，

sentences.en: and lots of stories, mostly shared on Reddit,
sentences.zh: 还有许多故事，大多在红迪网上分享，

sentences.en: of encounters with ghost trains passing by filled with alien creatures.
sentences.zh: 讲述了偶遇幽灵列车驶过且车厢里挤满了外星生物的经历。

sentences.en: And while it's mostly playful,
sentences.zh: 虽然这大多只是开玩笑，

sentences.en: there is something about the metro's design that lends itself to being an imaginative space for its passengers.
sentences.zh: 但地铁设计的某些特点确实让它成为了乘客发挥想象力的空间。

sentences.en: Zachary Schrag hasn't personally seen any aliens on the metro,
sentences.zh: 扎卡里·施拉格虽然没有亲自在地铁上见过外星人，

sentences.en: but he still kind of gets it.
sentences.zh: 但他还是有点理解这种感受。

sentences.en: And so when a train comes in, it casts a shadow up on the vault.
sentences.zh: 所以当列车驶入时，它会在拱顶上投下阴影。

sentences.en: So there's this, you know, dark shadow coming in and slowing down
sentences.zh: 所以你会看到，你知道的，一个黑影驶入并减速，

sentences.en: and then speeding up again as it disappears.
sentences.zh: 然后随着它消失又再次加速。

sentences.en: And here we are at the end of the longest escalator
sentences.zh: 现在我们来到了最长自动扶梯的尽头，

sentences.en: in one of the country's most iconic metro stations.
sentences.zh: 位于这个国家最具标志性的地铁站之一。

sentences.en: Thanks, Olivia.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，奥利维亚。

sentences.en: This was great.
sentences.zh: 这期节目太棒了。

sentences.en: A few months back, a story went around the internet
sentences.zh: 几个月前，网上流传着一个故事，

sentences.en: about a bizarre computer issue from the mid-2000s.
sentences.zh: 关于2005年中期的一个离奇电脑故障。

sentences.en: It was from a blog post by Microsoft developer Raymond Chen.
sentences.zh: 它源于微软开发者雷蒙德·陈的一篇博客文章。

sentences.en: So a laptop manufacturer came to the Windows team
sentences.zh: 当时一家笔记本电脑制造商找到Windows团队，

sentences.en: and reported a serious problem.
sentences.zh: 并报告了一个严重的问题。

sentences.en: It turns out when they played a song by one specific artist,
sentences.zh: 原来，当他们播放某位特定歌手的歌曲时，

sentences.en: and in fact it was one specific song,
sentences.zh: 确切地说，是一首特定的歌曲，

sentences.en: the laptop crashed.
sentences.zh: 笔记本电脑就会崩溃。

sentences.en: But things got even weirder when they started testing it out.
sentences.zh: 但当他们开始进行测试时，事情变得更加诡异了。

sentences.en: They found that this song crashed some of their competitors' laptops also.
sentences.zh: 他们发现这首歌也会导致他们某些竞争对手的笔记本电脑崩溃。

sentences.en: But the weirdest thing was that if you played this song,
sentences.zh: 但最奇怪的是，如果你播放这首歌，

sentences.en: it not only crashed the laptop that was playing it,
sentences.zh: 它不仅会使正在播放的笔记本电脑崩溃，

sentences.en: it also crashed a laptop that was sitting next to it
sentences.zh: 还会使旁边放着的一台根本没有播放这首歌的笔记本电脑

sentences.en: that wasn't playing the song at all.
sentences.zh: 也一起崩溃。

sentences.en: Now, before I play this song,
sentences.zh: 现在，在我播放这首歌之前，

sentences.en: if you have a laptop that's over 15 years old,
sentences.zh: 如果你有一台用了超过15年的笔记本电脑，

sentences.en: you might want to cover its ears.
sentences.zh: 你可能得帮它捂捂耳朵。

sentences.en: This is Janet Jackson's 1989 smash hit, Rhythm Nation.
sentences.zh: 这是珍妮·杰克逊1989年的热门金曲《Rhythm Nation》。

sentences.en: Now, I found this story fascinating and bizarre,
sentences.zh: 我发现这个故事既迷人又离奇，

sentences.en: but even after reading the blog post,
sentences.zh: 但即使在读完那篇博客文章之后，

sentences.en: I still didn't really understand what was going on,
sentences.zh: 我还是不太明白到底是怎么回事，

sentences.en: so I asked our engineer, Martin Gonzalez, to come explain.
sentences.zh: 所以我请我们的工程师马丁·冈萨雷斯来解释一下。

sentences.en: Hey, Roman, what's up?
sentences.zh: 嘿，罗曼，怎么啦？

sentences.en: Hey.
sentences.zh: 嘿。

sentences.en: So what do you have for me?
sentences.zh: 你给我带来了什么？

sentences.en: Okay, well, disclaimer up front,
sentences.zh: 好吧，先声明一下，

sentences.en: I'm a music school dropout, not a computer scientiSt.
sentences.zh: 我是音乐学院的辍学生，可不是计算机科学家。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I wouldn't have it any other way.
sentences.zh: 我可求之不得呢。

sentences.en: So here's my best understanding of what happened.
sentences.zh: 所以我把我对这件事的理解讲一讲。

sentences.en: These engineers were trying to figure out
sentences.zh: 这些工程师当时在试图弄清楚

sentences.en: how this particular song was crashing all these different computers,
sentences.zh: 为什么这首歌能让这么多不同的电脑崩溃，

sentences.en: and they narrowed it down to the hard drive.
